newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stake in Germany's Bewag may go abroad -- official.
newsitem.headline: Stake in Germany's Bewag may go abroad -- official.

text.p: A senior Berlin government official at the weekend raised chances for a stake in state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag) to be sold to foreign investors, saying she preferred such a step.

Annette Fugmann-Heesing, finance minister for the state of Berlin, told German radio that the city should sell its entire stake in Bewag to a foreign group "because we could attract international investors this way."
The state of Berlin currently holds a 50.8 percent stake in Bewag. PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk each hold a 10 percent stake and the rest of Bewag's shares are owned by a other shareholders.

Fugmann-Heesing said the state was eager to attract an investor who had a long-term strategic interest in the group. "We do not want someone who is purely interested in this as financial investment," she said.
Late last week, German utilities Viag AG and Veba were said to be interested in making a joint bid for a higher stake in Bewag.

On Thursday, Viag confirmed it was interested in increasing its stake in Bewag. Viag and Veba each already own 10 percent of Bewag's capital via subsidiaries and control 14 percent of its voting rights.
Sources on Friday said that nine of the 28 interested parties in Bewag were still in the running.
Other groups, including British electricity generator PowerGen Plc, have also expressed an interest in Bewag.
Meanwhile German newspaper Der Tagesspiegel said that the chances for a foreign investor to take the stake were falling.
The paper reported that U.S. group Enron Corp pulled out of the running on Friday.
